category: Multibody Dynamics Module: joints, joint properties, rigid-body features, gears, chains and the Lumped Mechanical System
description: Features of the Multibody Dynamics (mbd) and Joints interfaces: all joint types with their elasticity, constraints, locking, springs, prescribed motion, applied loads and friction; base motion, measurement, rigid body contact and cam-follower; spur/helical/bevel/worm gears and racks with gear pairs, mesh elasticity, transmission error, backlash and friction; chain drives and geometry parts; FSI and rotating-machinery couplings; and the Lumped Mechanical System (lms) circuit-style interface. Type strings and parameter keys shown in Java were confirmed in COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Joints (joints)
tools.description: Lightweight interface that provides the joint features of Multibody Dynamics (hinge, prismatic, ball, fixed, etc. with elasticity, friction, locking) to connect structural components modeled in Solid Mechanics, Shell or Beam through Attachments, without turning the model into a multibody system. Use it for static or dynamic structures whose parts are connected by mechanical joints (door hinges, pinned frames); use Multibody Dynamics for true mechanism dynamics.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Joints. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("joints", "Joints", "geom1"); physics("joints").create("hgj1", "HingeJoint", -1).

parameters.name: Joint nodes
parameters.description: Same joint types and subnodes as in Multibody Dynamics.

parameters.name: Attachments
parameters.description: Defined in the connected structural interfaces (Solid, Shell edges, Beam points).

tools.notes: Requires the Multibody Dynamics Module. See also the existing Multibody Dynamics (mbd) entry.

tools.name: Prismatic Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Translational (sliding) joint with one relative translational degree of freedom along the joint axis between a source and destination (Attachment, Rigid Material, gear, rack, Base Motion or Fixed). The center of joint can be the centroid of source/destination/selected entities or user defined; the axis comes from a direction, a parallel edge or a coordinate system. Subnodes add constraints, locking, springs and dampers, prescribed motion, applied force and friction; joint forces can be computed with weak constraints.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Prismatic Joint. Java: physics("mbd").create("prj1", "PrismaticJoint", -1); set("Source", "fixed" | "rd1" | "att1"); set("Destination", "rd2"); set("CenterOfJointType", "UserDefined"); set("AxisOfJointType", "SpecifyDirection"); set("e", new String[]{"0", "0", "1"}).

parameters.name: Source, Destination
parameters.description: Attachments, rigid domains, gears, Base Motion or fixed.

parameters.name: CenterOfJointType, xc, x_off
parameters.description: Joint center definition with optional offset.

parameters.name: AxisOfJointType, e
parameters.description: Joint axis direction or parallel edge (Joint Axis subnode).

parameters.name: JointElasticity, JointForcesAndMoments
parameters.description: RigidJoint or elastic joint; compute joint forces (e.g. via weak constraints).

tools.notes: Use Source/Destination filters in large models to narrow the attachment lists.

tools.name: Hinge Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Revolute joint with one relative rotational degree of freedom about the joint axis at the center of joint, the most common joint for linkages, crank mechanisms, doors, cranes and gear shafts (gear to housing). It supports all joint subnodes: Joint Elasticity, Constraints, Locking, Spring and Damper, Prescribed Motion (rotation or angular velocity), Applied Force and Moment and Friction (with hinge radius).
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Hinge Joint. Java: physics("mbd").create("hgj1", "HingeJoint", -1); set("Source", "rd3"); set("Destination", "hlg7"); set("CenterOfJointType", "CentroidOfDestination"); set("e", new String[]{"1", "0", "0"}).

parameters.name: Source, Destination
parameters.description: Connected bodies (attachment, rigid material, gear) or fixed.

parameters.name: CenterOfJointType
parameters.description: CentroidOfSource, CentroidOfDestination, centroid of selected entities (Center of Joint subnodes) or UserDefined.

parameters.name: e / Joint Axis
parameters.description: Rotation axis (in 2D always out of plane).

parameters.name: JointElasticity
parameters.description: RigidJoint or elastic (adds a Joint Elasticity subnode).

tools.notes: Joint rotation and moment variables such as mbd.hgj1.th are available for results and control expressions.

tools.name: Cylindrical Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Joint with one translational and one rotational degree of freedom along/about the same axis, equivalent to a prismatic plus hinge joint: shafts sliding in bushings, telescopic struts, hydraulic cylinders that can rotate. Both motions can be constrained, locked, sprung, prescribed or given friction (with cylinder radius).
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Cylindrical Joint. Java: physics("mbd").create("clj1", "CylindricalJoint", -1); set("JointType", "Cylindrical") is implied by the type.

parameters.name: Source, Destination, center, axis
parameters.description: As for the Prismatic Joint.

parameters.name: Subnodes
parameters.description: Joint Elasticity, Constraints, Locking, Spring and Damper, Prescribed Motion (translational and rotational), Applied Force and Moment, Friction.

tools.notes: Prescribed Motion can set translation and rotation independently, each Always, Conditionally or Never active.

tools.name: Screw Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: 3D joint in which relative rotation about and translation along the axis are linked through the thread pitch and number of starts, so it has effectively one degree of freedom. It models lead screws, ball screws, jacks and threaded adjusters, and supports the usual joint subnodes including friction with a screw radius.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Screw Joint (3D).

parameters.name: Pitch p, Start n
parameters.description: Thread pitch and number of starts (lead = n*p).

parameters.name: Source, Destination, center, axis
parameters.description: As for other joints.

tools.example:
Multibody Dynamics > Screw Joint 1: Source = Fixed (housing), Destination = Rigid Material 2 (screw)
Pitch 5[mm], Start 1
Prescribed Motion: angular velocity 2*pi[rad/s] -> nut advances 5 mm/s
tools.notes: Friction in the thread can be added with the Friction subnode (Screw radius).

tools.name: Planar Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Joint with two translational degrees of freedom in the plane perpendicular to the joint axis and one rotation about that axis, representing a body sliding on a surface (feet of a washing machine on the floor, swashplate interfaces). Friction can be a total force at the joint center or distributed over selected boundaries (Contact Area subnode), and constraints can be axial or radial.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Planar Joint. Java: physics("mbd").create("plj1", "PlanarJoint", -1); feature("plj1").create("fric1", "Friction", -1); feature("plj1").feature("fric1").set("FrictionModel", "TotalForceAtCenterOfJoint").

parameters.name: e
parameters.description: Joint axis (plane normal).

parameters.name: Friction model
parameters.description: Total force at center of joint or distributed force on selected boundaries.

parameters.name: Constraints
parameters.description: Axial or radial constraint type with limits.

tools.notes: Unilateral contact (lift-off) is not modeled by a planar joint; use Rigid Body Contact or structural contact for that.

tools.name: Ball Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Spherical joint with three relative rotational degrees of freedom about the center of joint and no relative translation, used for suspension ball joints, robot wrists and linkage ends. Rotations can be restrained with inclination-angle and axial-rotation constraints, locking, springs and dampers, prescribed motion and friction (ball radius).
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Ball Joint. Java: physics("mbd").create("blj1", "BallJoint", -1); set("Source", "rd2"); set("Destination", "rd7"); set("CenterOfJointType", "CentroidOfSelectedEntities").

parameters.name: Center of joint
parameters.description: Point about which the bodies rotate (Center of Joint subnodes for entity centroids).

parameters.name: e, ed
parameters.description: Reference axes used for inclination and axial rotation measures.

parameters.name: Subnodes
parameters.description: Constraints, Locking, Spring and Damper (inclination, axial), Prescribed Motion, Applied Force and Moment, Friction.

tools.notes: Rotational stiffness matrix inputs are not available in Joint Elasticity for ball joints (no rotational constraints).

tools.name: Slot Joint and Reduced Slot Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Slot Joint: three rotations plus one translation along the slot axis (ball joint sliding in a slot). Reduced Slot Joint: one rotation plus one translation with orthogonal axes (pin in a slot, crank-slider pins); in 2D the rotation axis is out of plane. The translational axis can be attached to the source or destination. Used for crane cylinders, slotted cams and slider mechanisms.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Slot Joint | Reduced Slot Joint. Java: physics("mbd").create("slj1", "SlotJoint", -1); physics("mbd").create("rslj1", "ReducedSlotJoint", -1); set("JointTranslationalAxis", "AttachedOnSource" | "DestinationAxis"); set("e_tr", ...); set("e_rot", ...).

parameters.name: JointTranslationalAxis
parameters.description: Translational axis attached on source or destination.

parameters.name: e_tr, e_rot (Reduced Slot)
parameters.description: Translational and rotational axes (orthogonal).

parameters.name: Subnodes
parameters.description: Joint Elasticity, Constraints, Locking, Spring and Damper, Prescribed Motion, Applied Force and Moment.

tools.notes: Friction subnode is not available for slot joints (use Planar/Prismatic or contact where friction matters).

tools.name: Clearance Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Connects two points on two bodies so they can rotate freely and translate relative to each other only within a clearance distance, enforced by a penalty contact when the gap closes. It models worn or loose pin joints and bearing play, producing impacts and rattling in time-dependent analyses.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Clearance Joint. Java: physics("mbd").create("crj1", "ClearanceJoint", -1); set("Source", "rd3"); set("Destination", "rd4"); set("c", "C"); set("pj", "1e9[N/m]").

parameters.name: Source/Destination connection points
parameters.description: Centroids of source/destination/selected entities or user defined points.

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Clearance.

parameters.name: pj
parameters.description: Penalty factor for the clearance constraint.

tools.notes: Use small maximum time steps to resolve impacts in the clearance.

tools.name: Fixed Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Rigidly connects two components without adding degrees of freedom, e.g. a gear to its shaft, a component to a moving frame or reduced flexible components in component mode synthesis (with Source/Destination filters). With Joint Elasticity it becomes a six-DOF elastic connection (bushings, mounts, bolted interfaces with finite stiffness).
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Fixed Joint. Java: physics("mbd").create("fxj1", "FixedJoint", -1); set("Source", "rd1"); set("Destination", "hlg1"); set("JointElasticity", "RigidJoint").

parameters.name: Source, Destination
parameters.description: Bodies to connect.

parameters.name: JointElasticity
parameters.description: RigidJoint or elastic (Joint Elasticity subnode with 6x6 stiffness/damping).

parameters.name: JointForcesAndMoments
parameters.description: Compute reaction forces in the joint.

tools.notes: In Solid Mechanics, Fixed Joint is also available for CMS reduced components (see Reduced Flexible Components).

tools.name: Distance Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Keeps the distance between two connection points constant, like a massless rigid link with ball joints at both ends, without adding degrees of freedom; a prescribed extension turns it into a telescopic link. Useful for tie rods, cables in tension approximations and linkage simplifications.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Distance Joint.

parameters.name: Source/Destination connection points
parameters.description: Centroid, selected entities or user-defined coordinates.

parameters.name: Distance / extension
parameters.description: Default keeps the initial distance; prescribed extension for telescopic behavior.

tools.example:
Multibody Dynamics > Distance Joint 1: Source = Rigid Material 1 (point A), Destination = Rigid Material 3 (point B)
Prescribed extension: 0.01[m]*sin(2*pi*t)
tools.notes: No rotational constraints are imposed.

tools.name: Universal Joint (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Hooke or Cardan joint transmitting rotation between two shafts with different orientations; the gimbal is not modeled, and the joint adds two relative rotations about the gimbal legs. Input and output shaft orientations are given by directions or parallel edges, and the non-uniform output speed of Cardan shafts is reproduced.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Joints > Universal Joint (3D), subnodes Input Shaft Orientation and Output Shaft Orientation.

parameters.name: e_i0, e_o0
parameters.description: Input and output shaft directions (defaults (1,0,0) and (1,1,0)).

parameters.name: Center of joint
parameters.description: Gimbal center location.

tools.example:
Multibody Dynamics > Universal Joint 1: Source = input shaft (Rigid Material 1), Destination = output shaft (Rigid Material 2)
Input shaft: Specify direction (1,0,0); Output shaft: (cos(30[deg]), sin(30[deg]), 0)
tools.notes: Two universal joints in series with proper phasing give constant-velocity transmission.

tools.name: Joint Elasticity (Multibody Dynamics Joints)
tools.description: Subnode added when a joint's Joint Elasticity is set to elastic: the degrees of freedom normally constrained by the joint become elastic, with translational and rotational stiffness matrices k_u, k_theta (optionally coupled k_uth, k_thu) and viscous damping matrices c_u, c_theta in the joint or another coordinate system. It models bushings, compliant hinges and flexible mounts; individual DOFs can remain rigid.
tools.usage: <Joint> > Joint Elasticity = Elastic joint (subnode JointElasticity, tag je). Java: feature("hgj1").set("JointElasticity", "ElasticJoint"); feature("hgj1").feature("je1").set("k_u", new String[]{...9 values}); set("c_u", ...).

parameters.name: ul1..ul3, thl1..thl3
parameters.description: Which constrained translations/rotations are elastic.

parameters.name: k_u, k_th, k_uth, k_thu
parameters.description: Stiffness matrices (3x3).

parameters.name: c_u, c_th, c_uth, c_thu
parameters.description: Damping matrices (3x3).

tools.notes: JointElasticity = ElasticJoint / RigidJoint confirmed in Application Library models (Hinge, Fixed, Planar joints and Chain Drive). For stiffness on the free DOFs use Spring and Damper.

tools.name: Constraints (Multibody Dynamics Joints)
tools.description: Joint subnode that limits relative motion between upper and lower bounds (translational, rotational, inclination angle or axial rotation depending on joint type), implemented with penalty stiffness and a maximum allowable time step to resolve impacts at the stops. Several Constraints nodes can be added; the most restrictive wins. Typical for end stops of cylinders and hinges.
tools.usage: <Joint> > Constraints. Java: feature("hgj1").create("ct1", "Constraints", -1); set("th_max", "pi/4"); set("th_min", "-pi/4"); set("rotationalConstraintParameters", "Automatic").

parameters.name: u_max, u_min / th_max, th_min
parameters.description: Translational or rotational limits.

parameters.name: Constraint parameters
parameters.description: Automatic or user-defined penalty factor (p_u, p_th).

parameters.name: dT_max
parameters.description: Maximum allowable time step when the stop is hit.

tools.notes: Unlike Locking, the joint can move back from the limit.

tools.name: Locking (Multibody Dynamics Joints)
tools.description: Joint subnode similar to Constraints, but once the relative displacement or rotation reaches the limit the joint is locked at that value (penalty stiffness plus damping), e.g. latches, detents, one-shot deployment mechanisms and power switches. If all DOFs are locked the attached components move as one body.
tools.usage: <Joint> > Locking. Java: feature("prj1").create("lk1", "Locking", -1); set("u_max", "1e20"); set("u_min", "-maxdisp"); set("translationalLockingParameters", "UserDefined"); set("p_u1", ...); set("p_u2", ...).

parameters.name: u_max, u_min / th_max, th_min
parameters.description: Locking limits.

parameters.name: p_u1/p_th1, p_u2/p_th2
parameters.description: Penalty stiffness and damping for enforcing the lock.

tools.notes: Defaults scale with mbd.<joint>.lk1.Eequ and the model diagonal mbd.diag.

tools.name: Spring and Damper (Multibody Dynamics Joints)
tools.description: Adds elastic and viscous forces or moments on the free degrees of freedom of a joint: translational (spring constant or force as function of extension mbd.<joint>.sd1.us, predeformation, damping coefficient), rotational (spring constant or moment as function of rotation ths), inclination angle and axial rotation for ball/slot joints. Several can be superimposed; typical for suspension springs, torsion springs, governors and door closers.
tools.usage: <Joint> > Spring and Damper. Java: feature("prj1").create("sd1", "SpringAndDamper", -1); set("SpringType", "kSpring"); set("k_u", "k"); set("c_u", "c"); rotational: set("RotSpringType", "krSpring"); set("k_th", ...); set("c_th", ...).

parameters.name: SpringType / RotSpringType
parameters.description: Spring constant or force/moment as function of extension/rotation (Fs, Ms).

parameters.name: k_u, u_0, c_u
parameters.description: Translational stiffness, predeformation and damping.

parameters.name: k_th, th_0, c_th
parameters.description: Rotational stiffness, predeformation and damping.

tools.notes: Nonlinear springs (e.g. bump stops) use expressions like ka*(mbd.hgj2.th<0).

tools.name: Prescribed Motion (Multibody Dynamics Joints)
tools.description: Drives a joint degree of freedom by prescribing its relative displacement or velocity (translational) and rotation or angular velocity (rotational), with an activation condition (Always, Conditionally with a deactivation indicator, or Never active for multi-DOF joints). It is the standard way to model motors, actuators and kinematic drivers; weak and unidirectional constraint options are available.
tools.usage: <Joint> > Prescribed Motion. Java: feature("hgj1").create("pm1", "PrescribedMotion", -1); set("PrescribedMotionThroughRotational", "Rotation" | angular velocity); set("thp", "2*pi*t"); set("ActivationConditionRotational", "alwaysActive" | "conditionallyActive"); set("i_thp", ...).

parameters.name: PrescribedMotionThroughTranslational, up / vp
parameters.description: Displacement or velocity.

parameters.name: PrescribedMotionThroughRotational, thp / omegap
parameters.description: Rotation or angular velocity.

parameters.name: ActivationCondition*, i_up, i_thp
parameters.description: alwaysActive, conditionallyActive (deactivation indicator) or neverActive.

parameters.name: WeakConstraints, UnidirectionalConstraints
parameters.description: Constraint implementation options.

tools.notes: Use the joint reaction moment variables to size motors from prescribed-motion analyses.

tools.name: Applied Force and Moment (Multibody Dynamics Joints)
tools.description: Applies forces and moments on the source or destination attachment of a joint (at the attachment center, joint center or a user point) or directly on the joint degrees of freedom (scalar force for prismatic, scalar moment for hinge, vectors for planar/ball joints), e.g. actuator forces, motor torques or external torques on a gear shaft.
tools.usage: <Joint> > Applied Force and Moment. Java: feature("hgj1").create("afm1", "AppliedForceAndMoment", -1); set("AppliedOnSelectedAttachment", "Joint"); set("Ms", "-T_ext*step1(t)").

parameters.name: AppliedOnSelectedAttachment
parameters.description: Source attachment, destination attachment or Joint.

parameters.name: PointOfApplicationType, xpa
parameters.description: Center of attachment, center of joint or user-defined location.

parameters.name: F, M / Fs, Ms
parameters.description: Vector loads or scalar joint force/moment.

tools.notes: Loads are interpreted in the selected coordinate system.

tools.name: Friction (Multibody Dynamics Joints)
tools.description: Coulomb friction in joints for time-dependent analysis, regularized by a characteristic slip velocity: the friction force/moment is mu times a normal force computed from joint forces, attachment reactions, an interference-fit pressure or a user value, with a hinge, cylinder, screw or ball radius converting it into a moment. Planar joints can distribute friction over a Contact Area.
tools.usage: <Prismatic/Hinge/Cylindrical/Screw/Planar/Ball Joint> > Friction. Java: feature("hgj1").create("fric1", "Friction", -1); set("mu", "0.1"); set("rh", "10[mm]"); set("NormalForceDefinedThrough", "JointForcesAndMoments").

parameters.name: mu, v0
parameters.description: Friction coefficient and characteristic slip velocity (default mbd.diag*1e-3[1/s]).

parameters.name: rh / rc / rs / rb
parameters.description: Hinge, cylinder, screw or ball radius.

parameters.name: NormalForceDefinedThrough, ContributionOfInterferenceFit
parameters.description: Normal force from joint forces/moments, attachment reactions, or interference-fit pressure.

parameters.name: FrictionModel (Planar)
parameters.description: TotalForceAtCenterOfJoint or distributed over selected boundaries.

tools.notes: Only effective in time-dependent studies.

tools.name: Initially Rigid and Consistent Initialization (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Initially Rigid treats selected flexible Linear Elastic domains as rigid during the consistent initialization of a time-dependent study, so flexible bodies do not deform while initial conditions are made consistent. Together with the Force initial values option (Consistent initialization) on rigid domains, gears and Initially Rigid, specific translations or rotations keep exactly the entered initial values while the rest of the assembly adapts.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Domains > Initially Rigid; Rigid Material/Initially Rigid > Initial Values > Consistent initialization = Force initial values. Java (rigid domain): feature("rd1").set("ConsistentInitialization", "Default" | force initial values); set("TotalRotation", "1").

parameters.name: Initial Values
parameters.description: From physics interface node or locally defined.

parameters.name: Consistent initialization
parameters.description: Default or Force initial values for translation along axes and total rotation.

tools.example:
Multibody Dynamics > Initially Rigid 1 (flexible crank domain)
Rigid Material 2 > Initial Values: angular velocity 100[rad/s], Consistent initialization: Force initial values (Total rotation)
Study: Time Dependent
tools.notes: See the existing Rigid Domain entry for Rigid Material settings.

tools.name: Base Motion (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Defines the prescribed displacement, velocity or acceleration of the ground to which an assembly is attached (vehicle chassis, shaking table, seat base); joints, springs and dampers select the Base Motion as their source instead of Fixed. Initial base displacement and velocity can be given for velocity/acceleration input.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Base Motion. Java: physics("mbd").create("bsm1", "BaseMotion", -1); set("BaseMotionType", "Acceleration"); set("ab", new String[]{"0", "vtt_in", "0"}).

parameters.name: BaseMotionType
parameters.description: Displacement (ub), Velocity (vb) or Acceleration (ab).

parameters.name: ub0, vb0
parameters.description: Initial base displacement and velocity.

tools.notes: Different from Base Excitation in Solid Mechanics, which applies a frame acceleration at all constraints.

tools.name: Measure (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Global node that defines relative quantities between a reference point and an evaluation point (geometric points or coordinates): relative distance, displacement, velocity and acceleration vectors in the global and a chosen coordinate system, plus any additional user expressions, all available through Result Templates. Handy for clearances, stroke of actuators or relative motion of linkage points.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Measure (select Reference Point and Evaluation Point).

parameters.name: Reference point, Evaluation point
parameters.description: One point each (Point or Coordinates).

parameters.name: Additional measurements
parameters.description: Table of extra expressions to evaluate between the points.

tools.example:
Multibody Dynamics > Measure 1: Reference point = boom tip pin, Evaluation point = load hook
Results > Add Result Template > Measure 1 (relative distance vs time)
tools.notes: Add several Measure nodes for different point pairs.

tools.name: Rigid Body Contact (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Efficient analytic contact between rigid bodies: the source is a rigid sphere or cylinder (3D) or circle (2D) and the destination a sphere, cylinder, plane or arbitrary shape (circle or arbitrary in 2D), with shape parameters from geometry or user defined and a penalty contact law; a Friction subnode adds Coulomb friction. Used for rollers in bearings and conveyors, balls, cams and hoops without meshed contact.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Rigid Body Contact (+ Friction). Java: physics("mbd").create("rbc1", "RigidBodyContact", -1); set("SourceShape", "Spherical"); set("Source", "rd7"); set("DestinationShape", ...); feature("rbc1").create("fric1", "Friction", -1).

parameters.name: SourceShape, Source, ShapeParaSource, rs
parameters.description: Rigid source shape, domain and radius (from geometry or user defined).

parameters.name: DestinationShape, Destination, rd
parameters.description: Destination type (spherical, cylindrical, planar, arbitrary/noncircular) and parameters.

parameters.name: Friction: mu, v0
parameters.description: Coulomb friction with regularization velocity.

tools.notes: Forces geometric nonlinearity in stationary and time-dependent studies.

tools.name: Cam-Follower (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Forces a follower point (centroid of selected entities or a geometric point, with optional offset) on one moving body to stay on a cam surface (boundaries) or curve (edges in 3D) of another body, creating a higher kinematic pair with penalty enforcement; the connection can be always or conditionally active (allowing lift-off), connection forces can be computed and friction added in transient analysis. Models radial, cylindrical and slotted cams.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Cam-Follower (+ Friction). Java: physics("mbd").create("cfc1", "CamFollower", -1); set("selType", "Boundary" | "Edge"); set("connPoint", "GeomPoint"); set("ConnectionState", "alwaysActive"); set("pc", ...).

parameters.name: selType, cam selection
parameters.description: Cam boundaries or edges.

parameters.name: connPoint, follower selection, offset
parameters.description: Follower point definition and offset from the cam.

parameters.name: ConnectionState
parameters.description: Always active or conditionally active (lift-off).

parameters.name: pc, ConnectionForce
parameters.description: Penalty factor and connection force computation.

tools.notes: Refine the cam mesh for smooth follower motion and accelerations.

tools.name: Spur Gear (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Rigid spur gear on selected domains (2D and 3D) defined by gear mesh (external/internal), number of teeth, pitch diameter and pressure angle, gear axis and center of rotation; it acts like a Rigid Material with Fixed Constraint, Prescribed Displacement/Rotation, Applied Force/Moment and Mass and Moment of Inertia subnodes. It meshes with spur/helical gears (Gear Pair), worms (Worm and Wheel) or racks (Rack and Pinion) if compatible.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Domains > Gears > Spur Gear. Java: physics("mbd").create("spg1", "SpurGear", 3); set("GearMesh", "External" | "Internal"); set("nt", "20"); set("dp", "40[mm]"); set("alpha", "20[deg]"); set("eg", new String[]{"0", "0", "1"}).

parameters.name: GearMesh
parameters.description: External or Internal.

parameters.name: nt, dp, alpha
parameters.description: Number of teeth, pitch diameter, pressure angle.

parameters.name: GearAxisType, eg
parameters.description: Gear axis direction or parallel edge (Gear Axis subnode).

parameters.name: CenterOfRotationType, InitialValueType
parameters.description: Center of mass or user defined; initial values from interface or local.

tools.notes: Gears are rigid; tooth compliance enters through Gear Elasticity on the pair. Gear geometries can be built from the Multibody Dynamics Part Library.

tools.name: Helical Gear (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Rigid helical gear (2D and 3D) with gear mesh type, number of teeth, pitch diameter, pressure angle and helix angle beta; the helix produces axial thrust in gear pairs. It connects to helical or spur gears via Gear Pair (including crossed-axis configurations), to worms via Worm and Wheel and to racks via Rack and Pinion.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Domains > Gears > Helical Gear. Java: physics("mbd").create("hlg1", "HelicalGear", 3); set("GearMesh", "External"); set("nt", ...); set("dp", ...); set("alpha", ...); set("beta", "20[deg]").

parameters.name: nt, dp, alpha, beta
parameters.description: Teeth, pitch diameter, pressure angle, helix angle.

parameters.name: GearMesh, eg
parameters.description: External/internal and gear axis.

tools.notes: Helical gears can also be used in the Solid Rotor interface of the Rotordynamics Module.

tools.name: Bevel Gear (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Rigid bevel gear in 3D defined by number of teeth, pitch diameter, pressure angle and cone angle, meshing only with another bevel gear through a Gear Pair (intersecting axes), as in differentials and right-angle drives.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Domains > Gears > Bevel Gear. Java: physics("mbd").create("bvg1", "BevelGear", 3); set("nt", "n_pn"); set("dp", "dp_pn"); set("alpha", "alpha"); set("gamma", "gamma_pn").

parameters.name: nt, dp, alpha
parameters.description: Teeth, pitch diameter, pressure angle.

parameters.name: gamma
parameters.description: Cone angle.

tools.notes: For the pair the Configuration is always parallel or intersecting.

tools.name: Worm Gear and Worm and Wheel (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Worm Gear models a rigid worm (3D) with number of starts, pitch diameter, pressure angle, lead angle and handedness; the Worm and Wheel pair connects it to a helical or spur wheel with non-intersecting, non-parallel axes (point contact), friction included by default, giving high reduction ratios and self-locking behavior.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Domains > Gears > Worm Gear; Global > Gear Pairs > Worm and Wheel (Worm = worm gear, Wheel = helical/spur gear).

parameters.name: n (starts), dp, alpha, phi
parameters.description: Worm starts, pitch diameter, pressure angle, lead angle.

parameters.name: Handedness
parameters.description: Right or Left.

parameters.name: Worm and Wheel: Friction
parameters.description: Added by default; Gear Elasticity, Transmission Error and Backlash optional.

tools.example:
Multibody Dynamics > Worm Gear 1: starts 1, dp 20[mm], alpha 20[deg], lead angle 5[deg], Right
Helical Gear 2 (wheel): 40 teeth
Gear Pairs > Worm and Wheel 1: Worm = Worm Gear 1, Wheel = Helical Gear 2, Friction mu = 0.05
tools.notes: Default gear axis of a worm is (1, 0, 0).

tools.name: Spur Rack, Helical Rack and Rack and Pinion (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Racks are rigid translating gear elements defined by pitch and pressure angle (plus helix angle for helical racks) and a rack axis; the Rack and Pinion pair connects a spur rack to a spur gear or a helical rack to a helical gear, converting rotation to translation, with point or line contact and optional elasticity, transmission error, backlash and friction.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Domains > Gears > Spur Rack | Helical Rack (Rack Axis subnode); Global > Gear Pairs > Rack and Pinion.

parameters.name: Pitch p, pressure angle alpha
parameters.description: Rack tooth geometry (helix angle for helical racks).

parameters.name: Rack axis e_r
parameters.description: Translation direction.

parameters.name: Rack and Pinion: Contact model
parameters.description: Point or line contact; gear pair property options.

tools.example:
Multibody Dynamics > Spur Rack 1: pitch 3.14[mm], alpha 20[deg], rack axis (1,0,0)
Spur Gear 1 (pinion): 20 teeth, dp 20[mm]
Gear Pairs > Rack and Pinion 1: Rack = Spur Rack 1, Pinion = Spur Gear 1
tools.notes: Gear pair compatibility criteria (module, pressure angle, helix) must be satisfied.

tools.name: Gear Pair (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Connects a wheel and a pinion (spur, helical or bevel) so that there is no relative motion along the line of action at the contact point, while other motions stay independent; line contact adds a constraint on relative rotation about the line joining the centers. The line of action is obtained by clockwise or counterclockwise rotation of the tangent depending on driver and rotation sign. Optional Gear Elasticity, Transmission Error, Backlash and Friction subnodes and contact force computation make it suitable for gearbox dynamics, rattle and noise.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Gear Pairs > Gear Pair. Java: physics("mbd").create("grp1", "GearPair", -1); set("Wheel", "hlg6"); set("Pinion", "hlg1"); set("ObtainedThrough", "ClockwiseDirection"); set("ContactModel", "PointContact"); set("IncludeGearElasticity", "1"); set("IncludeBacklash", "0").

parameters.name: Wheel, Pinion
parameters.description: Gear nodes forming the pair.

parameters.name: ObtainedThrough
parameters.description: Line of action by clockwise or counterclockwise rotation of the tangent.

parameters.name: Configuration, ContactModel
parameters.description: Parallel or intersecting / neither; PointContact or line contact.

parameters.name: IncludeGearElasticity, IncludeTransmissionError, IncludeBacklash, IncludeFriction
parameters.description: Enable the corresponding subnodes.

parameters.name: ContactForceComputation, pc
parameters.description: Contact force evaluation and penalty factor.

tools.notes: Gears must satisfy the compatibility criteria. Combine with Hinge Joints to the housing and Radial Roller Bearings for gearbox vibration studies.

tools.name: Gear Elasticity (Multibody Dynamics Gear Pairs)
tools.description: Subnode that makes the gear mesh compliant: mesh stiffness from tooth stiffness of the individual gears (functions of the mesh cycle, e.g. mbd.grp1.thm_wh) or total pair stiffness, constant (1, 2 or 3) or varying contact ratio with a maximum value, and mesh damping. The periodic stiffness variation is the main source of gear whine excitation.
tools.usage: Gear Pair / Worm and Wheel / Rack and Pinion > Include gear elasticity (subnode GearElasticity, tag gel). Java: feature("grp1").feature("gel1").set("Specify", "IndividualGears"); set("kt_dr", "kt"); set("kt_dn", "kt"); set("ContactRatioType", "Varying"); set("MaximumContactRatio", "2"); set("cg", ...).

parameters.name: Specify
parameters.description: IndividualGears (tooth stiffness of each gear) or total stiffness of the pair.

parameters.name: kt_dr, kt_dn / km_*, kf_*
parameters.description: Tooth stiffness values or mesh-cycle functions.

parameters.name: ContactRatioType, ContactRatio, MaximumContactRatio
parameters.description: Constant or varying contact ratio.

parameters.name: cg
parameters.description: Mesh damping.

tools.notes: Cannot be added or removed manually; controlled by the parent's checkbox.

tools.name: Transmission Error and Backlash (Multibody Dynamics Gear Pairs)
tools.description: Transmission Error prescribes the static transmission error (profile modifications, manufacturing errors) of individual gears or the pair as a function of the mesh cycle or full revolution, a key excitation for gear noise. Backlash adds a gap b_l in the mesh enforced with a penalty and optional time-step control, enabling gear rattle and impact simulations in time-dependent studies.
tools.usage: Gear Pair > Include transmission error / Include backlash (subnodes TransmissionError (ter) and Backlash (bcl)). Java: feature("grp1").set("IncludeBacklash", "1"); feature("grp1").feature("bcl1").set("bl", "50[um]"); feature("grp1").feature("ter1").set("Specify", "IndividualGears").

parameters.name: Specify, em_dr/ef_dr, em_dn/ef_dn
parameters.description: Transmission error per gear as mesh-cycle or full-revolution functions (or of the pair).

parameters.name: bl, pb
parameters.description: Backlash and penalty factor.

parameters.name: ManualControlOnTimeStepping, dT_max
parameters.description: Limit the time step during penetration.

tools.notes: Backlash only acts in time-dependent analysis.

tools.name: Friction (Multibody Dynamics Gear Pairs)
tools.description: Adds sliding friction forces between meshing teeth in the plane perpendicular to the line of action for Gear Pair, Worm and Wheel and Rack and Pinion, with friction coefficient, characteristic slip velocity and normal force from the computed contact force (or user value) and an optional maximum friction force. It captures efficiency losses and friction-induced excitation.
tools.usage: Gear Pair > Include friction (subnode Friction, tag fric). Java: feature("grp1").set("IncludeFriction", "1"); feature("grp1").feature("fric1").set("mu", "0.05"); set("NormalForceDefinedThrough", "ContactForce").

parameters.name: mu, v0
parameters.description: Friction coefficient and characteristic slip velocity.

parameters.name: NormalForceDefinedThrough, N
parameters.description: ContactForce or user-defined normal force.

parameters.name: Ffmax
parameters.description: Maximum friction force (default Inf).

tools.notes: Requires contact force computation in the parent pair.

tools.name: Chain Drive (Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Generates a complete roller chain-sprocket model in 2D or 3D: the Create Links and Joints button builds node groups of Rigid Material links (rigid, elastic or rigid with elastic bushing), Attachments, Hinge Joints (optionally elastic), sprocket rigid bodies and mounting joints, and sprocket-roller contacts (mesh-based or roller-center-based). Geometry and selections come from the Multibody Dynamics Part Library roller chain and sprocket parts.
tools.usage: Multibody Dynamics > Global > Chain Drive > Create Links and Joints (subnodes Sprocket Axis, Joint Elasticity). Java: physics("mbd").create("cdr1", "ChainDrive", -1); set("SelSettings", "SelFromPart"); set("PartSelection", "pi1"); set("LinkType", "ElasticLink"); set("SprocketType", "ElasticSprocket"); set("ContactMethod", "MeshBased" | "RollerCenterBased").

parameters.name: SelSettings, PartSelection
parameters.description: Selections from a part instance or manual selections.

parameters.name: LinkType, SprocketType
parameters.description: Rigid, elastic or rigid with elastic bushing links; rigid or elastic sprockets.

parameters.name: ContactMethod
parameters.description: MeshBased or RollerCenterBased sprocket-roller contact.

parameters.name: JointElasticity, SprocketJoint
parameters.description: Elastic link joints and sprocket mounting joints.

tools.notes: Click Create Links and Joints again after changing geometry or settings.

tools.name: Gear and Chain Geometry Parts (Multibody Dynamics Part Library)
tools.description: Parameterized geometry parts shipped with the Multibody Dynamics Module: gear tooth profiles (external/internal, rack tooth), spur gears (2D/3D, external/internal), helical gears (external/internal), bevel gear, worm gear, spur and helical racks, and roller chain, sprocket and complete roller chain-sprocket assemblies (2D/3D). Parameters are validated to avoid invalid gear geometry, and parts provide selections used by gear and chain drive features.
tools.usage: Geometry > Parts > Part Libraries > Multibody Dynamics Module > Gears | Chains, then insert as a Part Instance and set parameters (number of teeth, module/pitch diameter, pressure angle, face width, helix angle, etc.).

parameters.name: Gear parameters
parameters.description: Number of teeth, pitch diameter, pressure angle, helix/cone angle, face width, blank dimensions.

parameters.name: Chain parameters
parameters.description: Pitch, roller diameter, number of links, sprocket teeth.

parameters.name: Selections
parameters.description: Domain/boundary selections exported for physics setup (e.g. Chain Drive).

tools.notes: See the existing Part Instance / Part Libraries entry for general part usage.

tools.name: Fluid-Multibody Interaction (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Two-way coupling of Laminar (or turbulent) Flow with Multibody Dynamics, with an ALE moving mesh for the fluid: rigid or flexible bodies connected by joints move under fluid forces and move the fluid. The standard version is for union geometries (Fluid-Structure Interaction coupling); the Assembly version uses identity pairs and the Fluid-Structure Interaction, Pair coupling, more common for mechanisms.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Fluid-Structure Interaction > Fluid-Multibody Interaction | Fluid-Multibody Interaction, Assembly. Couplings Java: multiphysics().create("fsi1", "FluidStructureInteractionBC", 2) or multiphysics().create("fsip1", "FluidStructureInteractionPair", 2).

parameters.name: fsi / fsip coupling
parameters.description: Boundary coupling on shared boundaries or identity pairs.

parameters.name: Deforming Domain
parameters.description: Moving mesh (automatic remeshing may be needed for large motions).

tools.notes: Requires the Multibody Dynamics Module; turbulence requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: Magnetic-Rigid-Body Interaction in Rotating Machinery (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Combines Multibody Dynamics with Rotating Machinery, Magnetic and moving mesh features (3D and planar 2D) through the Magnetic Forces, Rotating Machinery coupling, so electromagnetic forces act on rigid or flexible rotor and stator parts connected by joints and bearings. It is used for motor vibration and noise, rotor eccentricity and electromechanical dynamics.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Rotating Machinery, Magnetic-Structure Interaction > Magnetic-Rigid-Body Interaction in Rotating Machinery. Coupling Java: multiphysics().create("mfrm1", "MagneticForcesRotatingMachinery", 2).

parameters.name: Magnetic Forces, Rotating Machinery
parameters.description: Force coupling between rmm and mbd.

parameters.name: Displacement discretization
parameters.description: Use second order in flexible domains when stresses are needed.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module in addition to the Multibody Dynamics Module.

tools.name: Lumped Mechanical System (lms)
tools.description: Circuit-style (0D) interface for mechanical systems built from lumped masses, springs, dampers, impedances and displacement/force sources connected between numbered nodes, with terminal nodes for boundary conditions (fixed, displacement, velocity, acceleration, mass, force, impedance). It supports stationary, frequency-domain, eigenfrequency and time-dependent studies and connects to finite-element structures via the Lumped-Structure Connection coupling, e.g. vehicle suspensions, human body models and loudspeaker drivers.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Lumped Mechanical System (default Fixed Node = ground). Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("lms", "LumpedMechanicalSystem", "geom1").

parameters.name: Two-port components
parameters.description: Mass, Spring, Damper, Impedance, Displacement Source, Force Source, External Source.

parameters.name: Terminal nodes
parameters.description: Fixed, Displacement, Velocity, Acceleration, Mass, Force and Impedance Node.

parameters.name: Subsystem Definition / Instance
parameters.description: Reusable, optionally parameterized subcircuits.

tools.notes: Node 0 is ground. The interface is also available with the Acoustics and MEMS products for lumped transducer models.

tools.name: Mass, Spring and Damper (Lumped Mechanical System)
tools.description: Basic two-port lumped components: Mass (m, initial displacement and velocity, optional exclusion from gravity), Spring (spring constant k and predeformation u0) and Damper (damping coefficient c), each connected between two node names. Results options add force, displacement, velocity and acceleration to default plots.
tools.usage: Lumped Mechanical System > Mass | Spring | Damper. Java: physics("lms").create("M1", "Mass", -1); feature("M1").set("m", "M_MD"); physics("lms").create("K1", "Spring", -1); feature("K1").set("k", "1/C_MS"); physics("lms").create("C1", "Damper", -1); feature("C1").set("c", "R_MS").

parameters.name: m, u, dudt, ExcludeGravity
parameters.description: Mass, initial displacement and velocity, gravity exclusion.

parameters.name: k, u0
parameters.description: Spring constant and predeformation.

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Damping coefficient.

parameters.name: Connections
parameters.description: The two node names of the component (0 = ground).

tools.notes: Set node connections in the Node Connections section (Java parameter Connections). Application Library: Multibody_Dynamics_Module/Tutorials/lumped_loudspeaker_driver_mechanical.

tools.name: Impedance and Sources (Lumped Mechanical System)
tools.description: Impedance connects a component defined by a mechanical impedance matrix Z between two nodes (frequency-dependent elements), Displacement Source imposes a relative displacement with phase, and Force Source a force with phase between two nodes, providing the excitations and generalized elements of a lumped mechanical circuit.
tools.usage: Lumped Mechanical System > Impedance | Displacement Source | Force Source (default names Z1, U1, F1).

parameters.name: Z
parameters.description: Impedance matrix elements.

parameters.name: u_src, phi
parameters.description: Displacement source amplitude and phase.

parameters.name: f_src, phi
parameters.description: Force source amplitude and phase.

tools.example:
Lumped Mechanical System > Force Source F1: nodes 0 and 2, f_src = BL*i_coil, phi = 0
Study: Frequency Domain 20 Hz - 20 kHz
tools.notes: Force Node and Displacement Node are the single-port (terminal) equivalents.

tools.name: Terminal Nodes (Lumped Mechanical System)
tools.description: Single-port nodes that set boundary conditions on a node of the lumped network: Free Node, Fixed Node (ground, default), Displacement Node (prescribed displacement and phase, or input from a Lumped-Structure Connection), Velocity Node, Acceleration Node, Mass Node (lumped mass to ground with initial values), Force Node (applied force and phase) and Impedance Node.
tools.usage: Lumped Mechanical System > Terminals > Fixed Node | Displacement Node | Velocity Node | Acceleration Node | Mass Node | Force Node | Impedance Node. Java: physics("lms").create("disp1", "DisplacementNode", -1); set("InputDisp", "UserDefined"); set("up1", "hb/2+wv1(t)"); physics("lms").create("frc1", "ForceNode", -1); set("fp1", ...).

parameters.name: InputDisp, up1, phi
parameters.description: Displacement input: user defined or from multiphysics coupling.

parameters.name: fp1
parameters.description: Force of a Force Node.

parameters.name: m (Mass Node), Z (Impedance Node)
parameters.description: Terminal mass or impedance.

tools.notes: Node names are set in Node Connections.

tools.name: External Source and Lumped-Structure Connection (Lumped Mechanical System)
tools.description: Couple a lumped network to finite-element structures: an External Source (two ports) or Displacement Node (one port) takes the displacements of connection points in a Solid Mechanics, Multibody Dynamics, Shell, Layered Shell, Membrane, Plate, Beam, Truss, Solid/Beam Rotor or Pipe Mechanics model, and the Lumped-Structure Connection multiphysics coupling applies the lumped reaction forces back to the FE model (e.g. tire/suspension subsystems on a multibody chassis).
tools.usage: Lumped Mechanical System > External Source (Input displacement = From multiphysics coupling); Multiphysics > Lumped-Structure Connection (Connect to = External source or Displacement node). Java: physics("lms").create("E1", "ExternalSource", -1); set("InputDisp", "Coupled"); multiphysics().create("lsc1", "LumpedStructureConnection", -1); set("LmsFeatType", "ExtSrcType"); set("LmsFeat", "E1"); set("Direction", "zAxis").

parameters.name: InputDisp
parameters.description: Coupled (from multiphysics) or user-defined port displacements up1, up2.

parameters.name: LmsFeatType, LmsFeat
parameters.description: Which External Source or Displacement Node is connected.

parameters.name: Direction / eu
parameters.description: Direction of the connection force/displacement.

parameters.name: Structure_physics, Lumped_physics
parameters.description: Coupled interfaces.

tools.notes: The coupling is global (entity dimension -1 in library models). Several External Sources (E1..E4) can each have their own coupling node.

tools.name: Subsystem Definition and Subsystem Instance (Lumped Mechanical System)
tools.description: Subsystem Definition groups components (including nested subsystem instances) into a reusable block with its own external node list and, with Advanced Physics Options, input parameters with default values. Subsystem Instance inserts the block into the main network, mapping its nodes and overriding parameters, e.g. four identical wheel/suspension subsystems in a vehicle model.
tools.usage: Lumped Mechanical System > Subsystem Definition (add components as subnodes) and Subsystem Instance. Java: physics("lms").create("sub1", "SubSystemBlock", -1); physics("lms").create("X1", "SubSystem", -1); feature("X1").set("subSystemName", "sub1").

parameters.name: Node Connections (definition)
parameters.description: Ordered external node names of the subsystem.

parameters.name: Input Parameters
parameters.description: Parameters and default values usable inside the subsystem.

parameters.name: subSystemName, Connections, paramValues (instance)
parameters.description: Referenced definition, main-system node mapping and parameter values.

tools.notes: Components in a subsystem may only connect to the subsystem's own nodes.
